# qualys Provider

Manage [Qualys](https://www.qualys.com/) VMDR configuration with Terraform: asset
groups, asset tags, vulnerability search lists and VM scan option profiles.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "qualys" {
  # Your subscription's platform API server. Required — there is no safe default.
  # Find it under Help > About in the Qualys UI, or at
  # https://www.qualys.com/platform-identification/
  # Can also be provided via QUALYS_URL
  base_url = var.base_url

  # Can also be provided via QUALYS_USERNAME
  username = var.username

  # Can also be provided via QUALYS_PASSWORD
  password = var.password
}
```

## Choosing the right `base_url`

Qualys hosts subscriptions on several platforms, each with its own API hostname
(`qualysapi.qualys.com`, `qualysapi.qg2.apps.qualys.com`, `qualysapi.qualys.eu`
and others). The provider will not guess: pointing at the wrong platform would
send your credentials to it. Set `base_url` explicitly.

## Authentication

The provider authenticates with HTTP Basic authentication, which every Qualys
API accepts.

Some subscriptions can additionally enable JWT bearer authentication (via
OpenID Connect or Qualys' own token endpoint), but it is opt-in per subscription
and must be activated by Qualys Support. The provider does not require it.

### The EULA trap

An API-only account — one with no UI access — stays inactive until the Qualys
EULA has been accepted, and **every** API call fails until then. If a brand-new
service account fails everything with an authorisation error, this is the most
likely cause. The provider detects it and says so explicitly.

## API limits

Qualys enforces per-subscription concurrency and rate limits. The provider
self-limits to the documented default of two concurrent calls per API, and waits
for the interval Qualys reports before retrying a blocked call.

Raising `concurrency` above the limit Qualys has actually granted your
subscription produces `HTTP 409` responses, not faster runs.

Destructive operations are never retried automatically, whatever `max_retries`
is set to: a blocked response does not prove the operation did not take effect,
and repeating a purge or delete on that assumption is not safe.

## API versions and deprecation

Qualys versions each API independently and runs an explicit deprecation
programme: a superseded version reaches End of Support six months after its
replacement ships, and End of Life six months after that.

The provider pins an API version per capability and logs a one-time warning when
it uses a capability that Qualys has since published a newer version for. Those
warnings appear in `TF_LOG` output — they are worth reading, because they are the
early notice of an endpoint that will eventually be decommissioned.

## Schema

### Required

- **base_url** (String) Qualys API server URL for your subscription's platform, for example `https://qualysapi.qualys.com`. Qualys hosts subscriptions on several platforms with different hostnames; find yours under Help > About in the Qualys UI, or at https://www.qualys.com/platform-identification/. This must be set explicitly — there is no safe default, and pointing at the wrong platform sends your credentials to it.
- **password** (String, Sensitive) Password for the Qualys API.
- **username** (String) Username for the Qualys API.

### Optional

- **concurrency** (Number) Maximum concurrent API calls. Defaults to 2, matching the documented per-subscription default. Raise this only if Qualys has raised the limit for your subscription; exceeding it causes HTTP 409 responses rather than faster runs.
- **max_retries** (Number) How many times to retry a call blocked by an API rate or concurrency limit. Defaults to 4. Destructive operations are never retried automatically regardless of this setting.
